events.summary: Speaker C presented the prototype: ergonomic, rubber, very simple, double curved, and different from other remotes.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: we wanted it to be ergonomic and to be made out of rubber

events.summary: Speaker C reported the thumb button is power, index finger is channel up, middle finger is channel down, ring finger is volume up and pinkie is volume down.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: Your index finger is channel up, middle finger is channel down

events.summary: Speaker C reported the big blue button is the lock button and the mute button is marked M.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: That's the lock button, has a L_ L_ on it and then the M_ is a mute button

events.summary: Speaker C reported a numeric keypad on top of the remote so users can key in a channel directly.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: there's a numeric keypad on the top so you can key directly to the to the channel

events.summary: Speaker A objected that the design would mean making both a right-handed and a left-handed remote.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: it'd mean we'd have to make a right-handed one and a left-handed one

events.summary: Speaker A said making left-handed and right-handed versions is a great idea.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: I think I think it's great, yeah, great idea.

events.summary: Speaker C reported that the main criteria from the last meeting was that the remote had to be chew proof.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: That was the main criteria from the last meeting, it had to be chew proof.

events.summary: Speaker A decided the group is going for the kinetic power.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: so we're going for the kinetic power

events.summary: Speaker A said the electronics are the simplest, easiest option inside the remote.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: we decided on it being just a simple, the easiest thing that's inside it

events.summary: Speaker A confirmed the case is double curved and made of rubber.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: So the case, we've gone for the double curved

events.summary: Speaker A confirmed the interface is push-buttons, with buttons in special colours and shapes.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: The interface is push-buttons. And button supplements well

events.summary: Speaker A stated the remote costs 10.70 Euros per unit to make, against a target under 12.50 Euros.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: That's gonna cost ten ten Euro seventy cents a unit to make

events.summary: Speaker A confirmed the remote is within budget, since the 10.70 Euros unit cost is under the 12.50 Euros target.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: So let's see if that comes within budget. And it does.

events.summary: Speaker C said the group is making a better profit than expected because production cost was saved.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: And we're actua actually making a better profit than we expected.

events.summary: Speaker D recorded the look and feel score as 1 on the 1-to-7 scale, meaning it fits the criteria.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: A one a one. So I'll just write criteria criteria one we get one

events.summary: Speaker C said the kinetic energy was the main technological innovation, and everything else was fairly simple.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: the fact that we used the kinetic energy was new

events.summary: Speaker D recorded the new technology score as 3 on the 1-to-7 scale, after the group debated two or three.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: three. So criteria three is is it easy to use?

events.summary: Speaker A gave the easy-to-use score as 2 on the 1-to-7 scale, because the remote is geared to right-handed people.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: Give it a t give it a two

events.summary: Speaker A gave the cost score as 1 on the 1-to-7 scale, because the remote is under budget.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: It's come in under budget. So that's a definite one.

events.summary: The group gave the amount-of-buttons score as 1 on the 1-to-7 scale, because it has only the necessary buttons.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: Contains only the necessary buttons. Yeah.

events.summary: Speaker D gave the repetitive strain injury score as 1 on the 1-to-7 scale, meaning it is very good against it.
events.speaker: D
events.quote: R_S_I_ is it good against? Yes. Very good. It's one.

events.summary: Speaker A said the remote will not easily get lost, and the group agreed a score of 2 on the 1-to-7 scale.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: I don't think it's gonna get lost easily.

events.summary: Speaker C recalled the earlier profit goal of 50 million Euros and questioned how to compute the profit now.
events.speaker: C
events.quote: It was fifty mil fifty million

events.summary: Speaker A said profit, selling and sales work goes to another department; this team only designs the product within budget.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: It gets handed over to another department

events.summary: Speaker A proposed marketing the remote as new, because it does the opposite of other remotes, which cause repetitive strain injury.
events.speaker: A
events.quote: our one does the complete opposite, you know, so that's something that's new
